title: Kernel of a degreewise epimorphism is quasi-isomorphic to the shifted cone
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and let $f:P\to Q$ be a morphism of cochain complexes of $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] such that $f^p:P^p\to Q^p$ is an epimorphism for every $p\in\mathbf Z$. Let $K\subseteq P$ be the termwise kernel, $K^p=\ker f^p$ with the restricted differential, and $\iota:K\to P$ the inclusion. With the mapping cone $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^r=Q^r\oplus P^{r+1}$, differential $(y,x)\mapsto(d_Qy+f(x),-d_Px)$, and the shift of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the complex $\operatorname{Cone}(f)[-1]$ has terms $Q^{p-1}\oplus P^p$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-d_Qy-f(x),\,d_Px)$. Then the maps $\kappa^p=(0,\iota^p):K^p\to Q^{p-1}\oplus P^p$ form a morphism of complexes $\kappa:K\to\operatorname{Cone}(f)[-1]$, and $\kappa$ is a quasi-isomorphism; in particular $K\cong\operatorname{Cone}(f)[-1]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$.

proof.text: Because $f$ is a morphism of complexes, $d_P(\ker f^p)\subseteq\ker f^{p+1}$, so the termwise kernels $K^p=\ker f^p$ with the restricted differential form a complex and $\iota:K\to P$ is a morphism of complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $k\in K^p$ the displayed differential of $\operatorname{Cone}(f)[-1]$ gives $d(0,\iota k)=(-f\iota k,\,d_P\iota k)=(0,\iota d_Kk)$ because $f\iota=0$; hence $\kappa=(0,\iota):K\to\operatorname{Cone}(f)[-1]$ is a morphism of complexes.

source.place: Definition 014Q (the cone differential and shift), together with the kernel-complex construction in the proof of Lemma 070M

proof.text: Let $Z$ be the complex with $Z^p=Q^{p-1}\oplus Q^p$ and differential $(y,q)\mapsto(-d_Qy-q,\,d_Qq)$ (this is $\operatorname{Cone}(\mathrm{id}_Q)[-1]$), and let $\pi^p:Q^{p-1}\oplus P^p\to Z^p$, $(y,x)\mapsto(y,f(x))$. Then $\pi$ is a morphism of complexes: $\pi d(y,x)=(-d_Qy-f(x),\,f(d_Px))=(-d_Qy-f(x),\,d_Qf(x))=d\pi(y,x)$. In each degree, $0\to K^p\xrightarrow{\kappa^p}Q^{p-1}\oplus P^p\xrightarrow{\pi^p}Q^{p-1}\oplus Q^p\to0$ is the direct sum of $0\to0\to Q^{p-1}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}Q^{p-1}\to0$ and $0\to K^p\xrightarrow{\iota^p}P^p\xrightarrow{f^p}Q^p\to0$, which is exact because $K^p=\ker f^p$ and $f^p$ is an epimorphism [def-sp-abelian]; so $0\to K\xrightarrow{\kappa}\operatorname{Cone}(f)[-1]\xrightarrow{\pi}Z\to0$ is a short exact sequence of complexes. The complex $Z$ is contractible: with $h(y,q)=(0,-y)$ one computes $dh(y,q)=(y,-d_Qy)$ and $hd(y,q)=(0,d_Qy+q)$, so $dh+hd=\mathrm{id}_Z$; hence $H^r(Z)=0$ for all $r$, the morphism $Z\to0$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $Q(Z)$ is a zero object of $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Definition 014Q (cone and shift); contractibility of the cone of an identity

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] applied to the short exact sequence of Step 2 there is a distinguished triangle $K\xrightarrow{Q(\kappa)}\operatorname{Cone}(f)[-1]\xrightarrow{Q(\pi)}Z\xrightarrow{\delta}K[1]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$. By TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] the triangle $K\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}K\to0\to K[1]$ is distinguished. The triple $(\mathrm{id}_K,Q(\kappa),0\to Z)$ is a morphism from the second triangle to the first: the first square is $Q(\kappa)\circ\mathrm{id}=Q(\kappa)\circ\mathrm{id}$, the second square consists of two morphisms into the zero object $Z$, and the third of two morphisms out of $0$. Its first and third components are isomorphisms ($Z\cong0$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ by Step 2), so by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] $Q(\kappa)$ is an isomorphism. Since $H^r\circ Q\cong H^r$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $H^r(\kappa)$ is an isomorphism for every $r$, i.e. $\kappa$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $K\cong\operatorname{Cone}(f)[-1]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$.
